subject: surgery
title: Chronic venous disease, CEAP classification, varicose veins, and endovenous ablation

steps.tx: Chronic venous disease arises from valvular incompetence and venous **hypertension** in superficial, deep, or perforating venous systems. When bicuspid venous valves fail, retrograde gravitational hydrostatic pooling transmits elevated pressures into cutaneous capillary beds. Extravasation of red blood cells produces hemosiderin hyperpigmentation, while pericapillary fibrin cuffs and chronic leukocyte entrapment induce progressive subcutaneous fibrosis termed lipodermatosclerosis. The medial lower calf and perimalleolar region represent the classic anatomical site of venous stasis.
steps.say: Chronic venous insufficiency stems from venous valvular incompetence and ambulatory venous hypertension. Hydrostatic pooling drives red cell extravasation, hemosiderin pigmentation, and subcutaneous lipodermatosclerosis over the medial lower calf.

steps.tx: The international CEAP classification categorizes venous disorders based on clinical, **etiological**, anatomical, and pathophysiological criteria. Clinical class C1 denotes telangiectasias or reticular veins. Class C2 encompasses true dilated, tortuous varicose veins measuring three millimeters or larger. Class C3 denotes lower limb edema without trophic skin changes. Class C4 includes pigmentation, eczema, and lipodermatosclerosis. Class C5 represents a healed venous ulceration, while class C6 denotes an active, open venous leg ulcer.
steps.say: The CEAP classification grades venous disease from C0 to C6. C2 represents varicose veins, C3 lower extremity edema, C4 trophic skin changes like lipodermatosclerosis, and C6 an active, non-healing venous leg ulcer.

steps.tx: Duplex ultrasound examination in the standing position represents the definitive diagnostic **investigation** for venous pathology. It documents anatomical venous pathways, identifies intraluminal thrombi, and quantifies retrograde reflux duration following distal manual compression release. Pathological reflux is defined as retrograde venous flow exceeding five hundred milliseconds in superficial and perforator veins, or exceeding one thousand milliseconds in deep femoral and popliteal veins. Deep vein patency must be confirmed prior to superficial interventions.
steps.say: Standing duplex ultrasound is the gold standard diagnostic test, identifying venous thrombi and quantifying reflux duration. Reflux exceeding five hundred milliseconds in superficial veins or one second in deep veins is pathological.

steps.tx: Conservative therapy utilizing graduated compression **stockings** exerting twenty to thirty or thirty to forty millimeters of mercury pressure constitutes initial management. For superficial axial incompetence involving the great saphenous vein, endovenous thermal ablation via radiofrequency or laser has replaced open high ligation and stripping as first-line therapy. Tumescent local anesthesia protects adjacent cutaneous nerves and absorbs heat during ablation. Ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy and cyanoacrylate adhesive provide effective non-thermal options.
steps.say: Graduated compression therapy provides foundational conservative support. Endovenous thermal ablation using radiofrequency or laser with tumescent anesthesia is the first-line treatment for saphenous reflux, replacing open surgical stripping.
